rationale: Evidence: iteration 6 is the best design so far (945.4). Oval, s-bend and slalom each finish 20/20, with progress about 0.996 and rms_error about 0.006. Iteration 7 (mass 0.5, base_speed 0.95) scored 941.6, lower. Its finish times rose (oval 2.23 s vs 1.99 s, slalom 2.79 s vs 2.57 s) and control effort went up, so the extra speed and lighter mass did not pay off. I therefore revert to the iteration 6 design. The remaining gaps are line-loss events (0.1 to 0.5 per run, about 15 points each) and completion time (about 2 points per 0.1 s). Steering gain is the one lever I have not tested on this geometry. Plan: keep the iteration 6 geometry and controller exactly, and change only kp from 4.5 to 5.0 (about 11% more steering authority). Expected result: fewer line-loss events and lower rms_error on the s-bend and slalom, with completion holding at 100%. Risk: more steering_oscillation on the oval, which is currently 0.21, so there is room. Hypotheses: H1, line losses come from the robot turning back too slowly on the sharper bends, so a higher kp reduces them. H2, if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 with no line-loss gain, kp is past its useful range and I should return to 4.5. Measurements wanted: line_loss_events, completion_time and max_error per track, plus steering_oscillation and control_effort to check whether the stronger steering adds jitter.
